clue.text: Right to go after bankrupt agent

indicators.note: going after something means being placed behind it, so this letter comes at the end

blocks.note: someone bankrupt is broke, out of money
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A permission to chase an insolvent representative, perhaps after a failed business.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent who arranges deals or sales on behalf of a client.

clue.text: Intensely cold beer

blocks.note: first meaning: of weather, piercingly cold
second meaning: a hoppy British ale

explanation.surface: A beer served at an icy temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a well-hopped British draught ale, so the clue reads like a pub order but holds two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind is a piercingly chilly one, and bitter is also a type of pale English ale.

clue.text: Clear above top of tower

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: above and over are synonyms
the first letter of tower

explanation.surface: Something visible high over the summit of a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plain to see, the same as clear or obvious.

clue.text: Stares at the old globes after end of lecture

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is taken
what comes after is placed second, so the selected letter leads the answer

blocks.note: the final letter of lecture
ye is an archaic spelling of the
globes are balls, round objects

explanation.surface: Someone gazing at antique globes once a talk has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: YE, as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe', is the old form of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Calmed down sailor on disastrous date

indicators.note: something disastrous has gone badly wrong, so the word's letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
taken as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman soothed after a romantic evening went badly.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm or anger has abated it has lessened and subsided, which is what calmed down means.

clue.text: Helplessly drunk, bishop before game

indicators.note: before means placed in front, so this piece starts the answer

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A bishop paralytic with drink before a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal British slang for extremely intoxicated, unable to stand.

clue.text: London street that nerds vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised things are wrecked and broken up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A city street that some geeks have defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a major street in central London running from Trafalgar Square towards the City.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a well-known thoroughfare in London's West End, home to the Savoy.

clue.text: Identify San Diego criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked and bent out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the city's name taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A witness asked to pick out a crook from San Diego.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify an illness or problem from its symptoms.

clue.text: Musical drama in which she (Greta Garbo) performed, receiving extremes of praise

indicators.note: performed hints at the letters being worked over and put into a fresh routine
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: taken as written
the actress's name taken as written
the first and last letters of praise

explanation.surface: A stage work in which the screen star Greta Garbo acted to critical acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes Garbo look like a note on who she is; in fact her name and 'she' are all fodder, plus the two outer letters of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera is a satirical musical play, so a musical drama.

clue.text: Fair exchange of repartee after somehow evading capture

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, inviting the letters to be arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written, its letters to be rearranged
to capture is to take

explanation.surface: Witty banter traded after someone has narrowly slipped arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Give and take is mutual concession or a lively back-and-forth exchange of remarks.

clue.text: Phones harsh critic for a box wrench?

blocks.note: to phone someone is to ring them
a critic who pans a show reviews it savagely

explanation.surface: A tough reviewer calls up to ask for a particular tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: box wrench is the American name for this tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring spanner has a closed loop end gripping the nut, which Americans call a box wrench.

clue.text: Additional passage from book court ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so these letters are dropped from the longer word

blocks.note: a quoted passage from a book is an extract
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A further excerpt from a legal volume that the judges disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra and additional are synonyms: more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Five in tug and ten lost in pontoon

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so its letters wander out of order

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Five people pulling on a tug-of-war rope, with ten more lost on a floating platform.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' looks like a container signal but is fodder. Pontoon is the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un is French for twenty-one and is the card game better known in Britain as pontoon.

clue.text: A Peebles spread cheese

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed and regathered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheese spread made in Peebles, a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like part of the food picture, a cheese spread, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel Paese is a mild, soft Italian cheese.

clue.text: Steal mate's porcelain

blocks.note: bone is old slang for steal
china, from rhyming slang china plate, means mate

explanation.surface: Pinching a friend's fine crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so a china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a type of fine porcelain made with bone ash.

clue.text: Fish, black when small

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
as and when are synonyms in 'as I left'
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fish that looks black while it is still young.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass is a spiny-finned sea or freshwater fish caught for food and sport.

clue.text: Son caught and punished

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
caught and trapped are synonyms

explanation.surface: A boy was caught and then disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: To be strapped was to be beaten with a leather strap as a punishment.

clue.text: Act up during search for reconnaissance vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to scour is to search thoroughly
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaving while out searching in an army scouting vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act up' reads as a phrase meaning misbehave, but 'up' acts alone on 'Act'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a fast, lightly armoured military vehicle used for reconnaissance.

clue.text: Fish, a freak, thrown back

indicators.note: thrown back means sent in the opposite direction, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
a nut is a crazy person or a fanatic, a freak

explanation.surface: An oddity of a fish returned to the water by the angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown back' fits the angling picture of releasing a catch, but it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, widely eaten.

clue.text: Forward subbed

blocks.note: first meaning: ahead of others in progress
second meaning: lent money ahead of payday

explanation.walkthrough: 'Subbed' looks like a sports substitution next to a forward, but it is British slang for lending someone money before they are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means progressive or ahead, and to advance cash is to sub someone a loan.

clue.text: Understood by few, British composer seen round about

indicators.note: seen round means wrapped around the outside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: An obscure British composer spotted wandering nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means secret or obscure, grasped by only a select few.

clue.text: Encourage operator to appear topless

indicators.note: without its top, a down entry loses its first letter

blocks.note: a surgeon is one who operates

explanation.surface: Urging a theatre surgeon to show up shirtless.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is to spur someone forward, the same as encouraging them.

clue.text: Discover arsenic? Sure

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
sure and certain are synonyms

explanation.surface: A detective checking whether a poison was arsenic, and being sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, to discover a fact.

clue.text: No power in golf club, say

indicators.note: no means without, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A golf club with no force behind it, as one might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' after the golf club, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or say something aloud.

clue.text: Fine German object

blocks.note: fine thread is thin
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A splendid German artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or article.

clue.text: Soldier's operation, not the NHS's concern

blocks.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
a practice is a professional business, as a doctor's operation

explanation.surface: An army private's surgery that the public health service did not handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service; 'operation' suggests surgery but means a business here.
explanation.definitionFit: Private practice is medicine paid for by patients rather than by the state health system.

clue.text: The person to give one a hand

definitions.text: The person to give one a hand

blocks.clueFragment: The person to give one a hand
blocks.note: surface reading: a helper who lends assistance
setter's reading: the one who hands out playing cards at the table

explanation.walkthrough: A 'hand' is the set of cards a player holds, so the helper is really the one distributing them.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the dealer distributes each player's hand.

clue.text: Mineral's exhausted, for the most part, in the Beaver State

indicators.note: for the most part means mostly, not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock; the 's is 'is'
exhausted supplies are gone

explanation.surface: Mining has largely run dry in a north-western American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon's official nickname is the Beaver State, after the animal's role in its fur-trading history.
